issues.claim: §5.2 F-RIVER's detection cell (l. 8771) reads 'descent stalls in a sink (`E_NO_PATH`, with the closest reached point, §3.1)'. Determinism's VDC0-27 added the clause this round from §3.1's former bracket [F-ROUTE, F-RIVER], while the kernel's VK0-11 fix narrowed that bracket to [F-ROUTE] (l. 3309). A river's course is traced by steepest descent (§4.2 S1 (3), l. 4888–4893), never by the path search, which alone returns E_NO_PATH (§3.1's path-search row, l. 3285). F-RIVER therefore names a code its stages never receive and contradicts the code's home (repair-r1-kernel.md cross-unit note 1).
issues.required_change: §5.2 F-RIVER, detection: replace 'descent stalls in a sink (`E_NO_PATH`, with the closest reached point, §3.1);' with 'descent stalls in a sink (§4.2 S1 (3));'. VDC0-27's other clauses stand.

issues.claim: Round 1 gave every raised way `feet: [RaisedFoot, RaisedFoot]` (§2.7, l. 2219, 2233–2238): 'the deck's two ends … where its ramps or stairs meet ground part 0 … so no document holds one without them'. §3.10's stored-references row (l. 4516) requires both feet. But §2.7 *At the frame* (l. 2526–2533) lays an aqueduct sourced beyond the frame 'up to the arena's outer ring, its deck ending there without a ramp', and a declared course drawn beyond the frame bends to the ring; T110-2 builds exactly that fixture (l. 17121–17124). At that end no ramp or stair meets part 0, so four things are undefined: the foot's ground end and its `raised_foot` vertex; the support step's L, measured 'between its two feet (where its ramps or stairs meet part 0)' (l. 2440–2441); §2.7's opening line, 'its two ends ramps or stairs joined to ground vertices' (l. 2438); and what a frame growth (§3.2 (9)), which strips the old ring, does to that end. The hard stored-references row then fails with E_INVARIANT at stage end on T110-2's fixture. This is the raised-way × frame combination (principle (11)), opened by this round's feet record.
issues.required_change: §2.7: in RaisedFoot's comment block after 're-placed by the way's re-derivation, one transaction per part (§3.4)', and in *At the frame* after 'its deck ending there without a ramp', add: 'At a deck end on the arena's outer ring — an aqueduct sourced beyond the frame, a declared course bent to the ring — foot i is that ring point: its ground end a `raised_foot` vertex placed by `splitThrough` on ground part 0's `margin` chain at the deck's end point, its deck end the spine's end on the part's own `margin` ring; no ramp or stair is drawn there. A frame growth (§3.2 (9)) extends the deck to the new ring as §4.11 continues a through-road, the raised way's re-derivation re-placing both ends of that foot on the new rings, one transaction per part (§3.4).' In the same section, l. 2438: replace 'its two ends ramps or stairs joined to ground vertices' with 'its two ends ramps or stairs joined to ground vertices, or an end on the outer ring (*At the frame*)'. In the support step (l. 2440–2441): replace 'between its two feet (where its ramps or stairs meet part 0)' with 'between its two feet (`RaisedWayRecord.feet`)'.

issues.claim: §3.4 *A layer's several arenas* (l. 3906–3908) says 'a raised way's two feet (`RaisedWayRecord.feet`, §2.7), where its ramps or stairs meet part 0 (item 110 (b))'. That restates where the feet lie, which is §2.7's to state, and contradicts §2.7 *At the frame*: a deck that ends on the outer ring has no ramp (VKr1-02).
issues.required_change: §3.4: replace 'a raised way's two feet (`RaisedWayRecord.feet`, §2.7), where its ramps or stairs meet part 0 (item 110 (b)), each a `raised_foot` vertex on part 0 and one on the raised part' with 'a raised way's two feet (`RaisedWayRecord.feet`, §2.7; item 110 (b)), each a `raised_foot` vertex on part 0 and one on the raised part'.

issues.claim: §4.1's `RaisedRead.feet` comment (l. 4625), 'the two part-0 vertices where its ramps or stairs meet the ground (§3.4)', repeats the same restatement. It contradicts §2.7 *At the frame* for a deck that ends on the outer ring (VKr1-02) and cites §3.4 instead of the record's home.
issues.required_change: §4.1 RaisedRead: 'feet: [PointCm, PointCm] /* the positions of the ground-part-0 ends of RaisedWayRecord.feet (§2.7) */'.

issues.claim: §3.3's KernelTx.expect (l. 3457) takes '§5.3's batch-scope invariants … the issuing stage's StageDecl.invariants of scope batch', and *Expectations* (l. 3488–3494) then rejects, repairs or downgrades on any failed entry. Round 1's §5.3 Invariant (l. 8823–8830) gives every row class 'hard'|'soft' ('hard: aborts the batch; soft (a statistics band): goes to the report'; likewise l. 8889–8890), and §3.1's E_INVARIANT (l. 3311) speaks of a hard invariant. A soft batch-scope entry, which the type admits, therefore has two outcomes: a rejected batch (§3.3) or a report line (§5.3).
issues.required_change: §3.3 KernelTx.expect comment: '… the issuing stage's StageDecl.invariants of scope 'batch' and class 'hard' (§4.12, §5.3; a soft row goes to the report, never into `expect`), the class floors of the faces it makes among them (§4.7's class-floor row); …'.

issues.claim: §7.4's frame row, regenerate cell (l. 10930): 'a rung change is a Re-derive from S0 and a population `adjust` one from S2 …, so a re-derivation never shrinks the frame below its protected content'. The frame's area follows the population (§3.2 (9)'s base law), and S1 lays the arena's outer ring from the frame (§4.1's S1 row, l. 4692). A Re-derive from S2 keeps S1's frame and can never recompute it. That contradicts the same row's lock cell, §7.1's bend.frame.held row (l. 10156), the round-1 sentence of §3.2 (9) (l. 3403–3405, 'A Re-derive that recomputes the frame — a rung change or a population `adjust` — reads this law afresh') and §7.1's Adjust rule (re-derive from the parameter's consuming stage, the earliest that reads it, §7.8).
issues.required_change: §7.4's frame row, regenerate cell: replace 'a population `adjust` one from S2' with 'a population `adjust` one from the population control's consuming stage (§7.8: the earliest stage that reads it — at the latest S1, which lays the frame from the frame law, §4.1's S1 row)'.

issues.claim: §2.2's Plat.frame comment (l. 567) reads 'set at creation; replaced only by the frame growth of an epoch's upward rung crossing (§4.11; J-A81.41), which only grows it'. That contradicts §3.2 (9)'s round-1 sentence (l. 3403–3405), §7.4's frame row and §7.1's bend.frame.held row: a Re-derive — a rung change or a population adjust — recomputes the frame by its law and may make it smaller, never below its protected content.
issues.required_change: §2.2 Plat: 'frame: Frame /* §3.2 (9): set at creation; replaced by the frame growth of an epoch's upward rung crossing (§4.11; J-A81.41), which only grows it, and by a Re-derive that recomputes the frame (a rung change or a population adjust), which never shrinks it below its protected content (§7.4's frame row) */'.
